Read Pearson's product-moment correlation coefficient r from GDC output

blocks.task_summary: Interpret the slope a in context: the average increase in waiting time per additional customer ahead.
method_path: Interpret a as the average increase in waiting time (minutes) per additional customer waiting ahead

evidence.basis: a represents the (average) increase in waiting time (0.805 mins) per additional customer (waiting to receive their coffee) R1

blocks.task_summary: Estimate Sarah's waiting time when x = 7 by substituting into the regression equation.
method_path: Substitute x = 7 into y = ax + b using their values of a and b

evidence.basis: attempt to substitute x = 7 into their equation (M1); 8.51693… ≈ 8.52 (mins) A1

blocks.task_summary: Find k such that the kth term of the arithmetic sequence with u1=60 and d=-2.5 equals zero.
Find the maximum value of S_n, the sum of the first n terms of the arithmetic sequence with u1=60 and d=-2.5.
method_path: Recognise that S_n is maximised when the last positive term is included (n = 25 where u_25 = 0)
accepted_alternatives: Express S_n = n/2(2×60 + (n-1)(-2.5)) as a quadratic, use GDC graph or table to find maximum sum = 750
Calculate S_24 = 24/2(2×60 + 23×(-2.5)) = 750 (symmetry gives same maximum at n=24)

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempting to express S_n in terms of n (M1); use of a graph or a table to attempt to find the maximum sum (M1); = 750 (A1). METHOD 2: recognizing maximum occurs at n=25 (M1); S_25 = 25/2(60+0), S_25 = 25/2(2×60+24×(-2.5)) (A1); OR attempting to calculate S_24 (M1); S_24 = 24/2(2×60+23×(-2.5)) (A1); THEN = 750 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find P(S ∩ T), the probability that a randomly selected student plays a sport and is involved in theatre.
method_path: Apply addition rule: P(S ∪ T) = P(S) + P(T) − P(S ∩ T)
accepted_alternatives: Use a clearly labelled Venn diagram with all values correctly placed

evidence.basis: EITHER P(S)+P(T)+P(S′∩T′)−P(S∩T)=1 OR P(S∪T)=1−0.18. THEN P(S∩T)=0.08 (accept 8%).

blocks.task_summary: Find P(T ∩ S′), the probability that a student is involved in theatre but does not play a sport.
method_path: Compute P(T ∩ S′) = P(T) − P(S ∩ T)
accepted_alternatives: Use a clearly labelled Venn diagram

blocks.task_summary: Find P(G ∩ T) given that 48% of students are girls and 25% of girls are involved in theatre.
method_path: Apply P(G ∩ T) = P(T | G) × P(G)

blocks.task_summary: Determine if events G (girl) and T (theatre) are independent, justifying the answer.
method_path: Compare with P(G ∩ T) = 0.12 from part (c)
Conclude not independent because P(G) × P(T) ≠ P(G ∩ T)
accepted_alternatives: Compare P(T | G) = 0.25 with P(T) = 0.20; since P(T | G) ≠ P(T), G and T are not independent

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: P(G)×P(T)=0.48×0.2=0.096. P(G)×P(T)≠P(G∩T)⇒G and T are not independent. METHOD 2: P(T|G)=0.25. P(T|G)≠P(T)⇒G and T are not independent. Note: Do not award A0R1.

blocks.task_summary: Find the range of the quadratic function f(x) = 6x² − 12x + 1 for x ∈ ℝ.
method_path: Attempt to find the vertex: x = −b/(2a) = 1 or complete the square to f(x) = 6(x−1)² − 5
accepted_alternatives: Use calculus: f′(x) = 12x − 12 = 0 → x = 1, f(1) = −5, range y ≥ −5

evidence.basis: attempting to find the vertex (M1); x = 1 OR y = −5 OR f(x) = 6(x−1)² − 5; range is y ≥ −5 A1

blocks.task_summary: Given (g∘f)(x) ≤ 0 for all x ∈ ℝ where g(x) = −x + c, determine the set of possible values for c.
method_path: Form the composite: g(f(x)) = −(6x² − 12x + 1) + c = −6x² + 12x − 1 + c
Identify the maximum value 5 + c at x = 1
accepted_alternatives: Discriminant method: For g(f(x)) = −6x² + 12x − 1 + c ≤ 0 for all x, require Δ ≤ 0: 144 − 4(−6)(−1+c) ≤ 0 → 120 + 24c ≤ 0 → c ≤ −5
Geometric transformation method: Reflect f vertically then shift by c; new vertex at (1, 5+c); require 5+c ≤ 0 → c ≤ −5

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (g∘f)(x) = −(6x²−12x+1)+c = −6(x−1)²−5+c (A1); relating to range of f OR attempting to find g(−5) (M1); 5+c ≤ 0 (A1); c ≤ −5 A1
METHOD 2: vertical reflection followed by vertical shift (M1); new vertex is (1, 5+c) (A1); 5+c ≤ 0 (A1); c ≤ −5 A1

blocks.task_summary: Show that the initial amount A₀ = 100 using the model A = A₀ e^(−kt) and the given condition that the plant has 100 units at time of death (t = 0).
method_path: Substitute t = 0 into A = A₀ e^(−kt)

evidence.basis: A₀ = 100e⁰ → 100 = A₀ AG [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Show that k = ln 2 / 5730 using the half-life of 5730 years, i.e. A(5730) = 50.
method_path: Substitute A = 50, t = 5730 into A = 100 e^(−kt)
accepted_alternatives: Substitute e^(−5730k) = 1/2, take ln to get −5730k = −ln 2 → k = ln 2 / 5730
Rewrite as e^(5730k) = 2, take ln to get 5730k = ln 2 → k = ln 2 / 5730

evidence.basis: correct substitution: 50 = 100e^(−k·5730) OR e^(−k·5730) = 1/2 (M1); EITHER −5730k = ln(1/2) (A1) and ln(1/2) = −ln 2 (A1); OR e^(5730k) = 2 (A1) and 5730k = ln 2 (A1); THEN k = ln 2 / 5730 AG. Note: Award full marks for at least two correct algebraic steps seen.

blocks.task_summary: Find the time for 25% of carbon-14 to decay (i.e. 75 units remain), correct to the nearest 10 years.
method_path: Substitute A = 75, k = ln 2 / 5730 into 75 = 100 e^(−kt)
accepted_alternatives: Use GDC to graph 75 = 100 e^(−(ln 2/5730)t) and find intersection, obtaining t ≈ 2378 then rounding to 2380

evidence.basis: 75 = 100 e^(−(ln 2/5730)t) (A1); EITHER using an appropriate graph to attempt to solve for t (M1) OR manipulating logs to attempt to solve for t (M1); t = 2378.164... → t = 2380 (years) A1

blocks.task_summary: Show that E(X) = (n+1)/(n+2) for the continuous pdf f(x) = (n+1)x^n on [0,1].
method_path: Set up E(X) = integral from 0 to 1 of x f(x) dx = (n+1) integral of x^(n+1) dx

evidence.basis: M1 for setting up E(X) = (n+1) integral of x^(n+1) dx from 0 to 1; A1 for evaluating to (n+1)/(n+2) leading to AG.

blocks.task_summary: Show that Var(X) = (n+1)/((n+2)^2 (n+3)) for the given pdf.
method_path: Compute E(X^2) = integral from 0 to 1 of x^2 f(x) dx = (n+1)/(n+3)
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Use Var(X) = integral of (x - mu)^2 f(x) dx directly. Expand (x - (n+1)/(n+2))^2, multiply by (n+1)x^n, integrate term by term from 0 to 1, and simplify to the same result.

evidence.basis: M1 for use of Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2; A1 for correct algebraic setup with integrals; M1 for algebraic manipulation to common denominator; A1 for final result AG. METHOD 2 shown as equivalent alternative with same mark allocation.

blocks.task_summary: Count the number of finishing orders of 8 runners where Jack finishes immediately after Andrea.
method_path: Treat Jack and Andrea as a single ordered unit

evidence.basis: Jack and Andrea finish in that order (as a unit) so we are considering the arrangement of 7 objects (M1); 7! = 5040 ways A1

blocks.task_summary: Count the number of finishing orders of 8 runners where Jack finishes in any position after Andrea.
method_path: Note symmetry: Andrea-before-Jack and Jack-before-Andrea are equally likely
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Fix the 6 other runners in 6! = 720 ways. For a given ordering of the 6, count acceptable positions for Jack relative to Andrea: sum 7+6+5+4+3+2+1 = 28. Multiply: 28 x 6! = 20160.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: the number of ways that Andrea finishes in front of Jack is equal to the number of ways that Jack finishes in front of Andrea (M1); total number of ways is 8! (A1); 8!/2 = 20160 ways A1. METHOD 2: the other six runners can finish in 6! = 720 ways (A1); when Andrea finishes first, Jack can finish in 7 different positions... 7+6+5+4+3+2+1 = 28 ways (A1); hence there are (7+6+5+4+3+2+1) x 6! ways = 28 x 6! = 20160 ways A1.

blocks.task_summary: Show that the real part of (1+z)/(1−z) equals zero, given z = cos θ + i sin θ, by rationalising the denominator using its complex conjugate, expanding, extracting the real part, and simplifying with cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.
method_path: Express (1+z)/(1−z) as (1+cos θ+i sin θ)/(1−cos θ−i sin θ)
Multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator (1−cos θ+i sin θ)
Expand the numerator: (1+cos θ + i sin θ)(1−cos θ + i sin θ)
Extract the real part of the numerator: 1−cos²θ−sin²θ
Apply cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 to simplify the numerator to 0

evidence.basis: M1: attempt to use the complex conjugate of their denominator. A1: correct conjugate expression with (1−cos θ + i sin θ). M1A1: expanding numerator and denominator — M1 for expanding, A1 for correct numerator (1−cos²θ−sin²θ). (M1): using cos²θ+sin²θ=1 to simplify numerator to zero. AG concludes the proof. Total [5 marks].

blocks.task_summary: Write the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (1 + t)^(-1) in ascending powers of t.
method_path: Write first three terms: 1 - t + t^2
accepted_alternatives: Accept the three terms listed as 1, -t, and t^2

evidence.basis: 9.(a) 1 - t + t^2 A1. Note: Accept 1, -t and t^2. [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Show that the Maclaurin series for sec x up to and including the term in x^4 is 1 + x^2/2 + 5x^4/24, using the Maclaurin series for cos x and the binomial expansion from part (a).
method_path: Write Maclaurin series for cos x: 1 - x^2/2! + x^4/4! - ...
Express sec x = (cos x)^(-1) and set t = cos x - 1 = -x^2/2 + x^4/24 - ...
Substitute t and expand: 1 - (-x^2/2 + x^4/24) + (-x^2/2 + x^4/24)^2
accepted_alternatives: Use sec x = 1 - (cos x - 1) + (cos x - 1)^2 - ... directly without explicit t-substitution

blocks.task_summary: Find lim(x→0) (x arctan(2x))/(sec x - 1) using the Maclaurin series for arctan x and the series for sec x from part (b).
method_path: Write Maclaurin series for arctan(2x) with 2x substituted: 2x - (2x)^3/3 + ...
Multiply by x to obtain numerator: 2x^2 - 8x^4/3 + ...
Write denominator sec x - 1 from part (b): x^2/2 + 5x^4/24 + ...

evidence.basis: 9.(c) arctan(2x) = 2x - (2x)^3/3 + ... (M1, with note: Do not award M1 unless x is replaced by 2x in arctan). Ratio set up and simplified to (2x^2 - 8x^4/3 + ...)/(x^2/2 + 5x^4/24 + ...) (A1). Final simplification to 4 (A1). [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find the standard deviation σ given that 2% of flight times exceed 82 minutes, where T ~ N(75, σ²).
method_path: Use inverse normal to find z-score for upper tail area 0.02

blocks.task_summary: Find P(T > 80) for T ~ N(75, σ²) using the σ from part (a).

evidence.basis: evidence of identifying the correct area under the normal curve (M1); P(T > 80) = 0.071193... = 0.0712 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find P(T < 82 | T > 80), the conditional probability that a flight taking longer than 80 minutes takes less than 82 minutes.
method_path: Recognise that P(80 < T < 82) is required

blocks.task_summary: Find the expected number of flights out of 64 that will have a flight time of more than 80 minutes.
method_path: Recognise binomial model X ~ B(64, p) with p = P(T > 80)

evidence.basis: recognition of binomial probability (M1); X ~ B(64, 0.071193...) or E(X) = 64 × 0.071193... (A1); E(X) = 4.556353... = 4.56 flights A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the probability that more than 6 of the 64 flights have a flight time exceeding 80 minutes.
method_path: Compute P(X ≤ 6) ≈ 0.83088 using binomial cumulative distribution

blocks.task_summary: Show that the volume of the solid of revolution formed by rotating the region enclosed by y=f(x), the axes, and x=ln 16 about the x-axis is πk²·15/34 cubic units.
method_path: Apply volume of revolution formula V=π∫[f(x)]²dx from x=0 to x=ln16
Substitute f(x)=ke^(x/2)/(1+e^x) and square to obtain integrand k²e^x/(1+e^x)²
Integrate using substitution u=1+e^x (or u=e^x, or by recognition)
accepted_alternatives: Integration by recognition (no explicit substitution)
Substitution u=1+e^x
Substitution u=e^x

evidence.basis: M1 for attempt to use V=π∫(f(x))²dx; M1 for integration method (by recognition or substitution); A3/A1 for correct antiderivative and integration steps; A1 for evaluating limits; final AG for πk²·15/34

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of k such that the bowl volume equals 300 cm³.
accepted_alternatives: GDC numerical solve feature

evidence.basis: M1 for valid algebraic or graphical attempt to find k; A1 for k=√(680/π)=2√(170/π) with k∈ℝ⁺

blocks.task_summary: Find OA=f(0) and BC=f(ln 16), the cross-sectional radii at the top and base of the bowl.
method_path: (i) OA = f(0): substitute x=0 into f(x)=ke^(x/2)/(1+e^x) to obtain k/2; then substitute k=√(680/π) to get OA=√(170/π)≈7.36 cm
(ii) BC = f(ln16): substitute x=ln16 to obtain k·4/17; then substitute k to get BC=8√(170)/(17√π)≈3.46 cm

evidence.basis: M1 for OA=f(0)=k/2; A1 for OA=√(170/π); M1 for BC=f(ln16)=4k/17; A1 for BC=8√(170)/(17√π)

blocks.task_summary: Find where the cross-sectional radius is decreasing most rapidly by sketching f'(x) or f''(x), and state the radius at that point.
method_path: Sketch graph of f'(x) to locate its minimum OR sketch f''(x) and identify where f''(x)=0
accepted_alternatives: Sketch f'(x) and find its local minimum
Sketch f''(x) and find where f''(x)=0 (maximum rate of decrease)

evidence.basis: M1 for recognising to graph f'(x) or f''(x); A1 for correct derivative expression; A1 for correct graph features (minimum of f' or x-intercept of f''); A1 for x=ln(2+√3); M1 for evaluating f at this x; A1 for radius=√(85/π)≈5.20 cm

blocks.task_summary: Show that f(x)=arcsin((1-x^2)/(1+x^2)) is an even function.
accepted_alternatives: Sketch graph of y=f(x) with line symmetry in the y-axis indicated

evidence.basis: EITHER f(-x)=arcsin((1-(-x)^2)/(1+(-x)^2))=arcsin((1-x^2)/(1+x^2))=f(x) R1 OR a sketch graph with line symmetry in the y-axis indicated R1. THEN f(x) is an even function AG. [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: By considering limits as x approaches +/-infinity, show that y=f(x) has a horizontal asymptote and state its equation.
method_path: Take limit as x->+/-inf of (1-x^2)/(1+x^2) equals -1

evidence.basis: as x->+/-inf, f(x)->arcsin(1)->pi/2 A1. horizontal asymptote is y=pi/2 A1. [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: (i) Show f'(x)=2x/(|x|(1+x^2)) for x not zero using quotient and chain rules. (ii) Using sqrt(x^2)=|x|, show f is decreasing for x<0.
method_path: Apply quotient rule to (1-x^2)/(1+x^2) to get 4x/(1+x^2)^2
Apply chain rule for arcsin(u) with u=(1-x^2)/(1+x^2)
For x<0, substitute |x|=-x to get f'(x)=-2/(1+x^2)
Note numerator negative, denominator positive, so f'(x)<0
Conclude f is decreasing for x<0

evidence.basis: (i) M1 quotient rule. A1 d/dx[(1-x^2)/(1+x^2)]=4x/(1+x^2)^2. M1 chain rule. M1 combining. A1 simplification. A1 f'(x)=2x/(|x|(1+x^2)) AG. (ii) EITHER for x<0, |x|=-x (A1) so f'(x)=-2/(1+x^2) A1 OR x<0 and 1+x^2>0 A1, 2x<0, |x|>0 A1. THEN f'(x)<0 R1. [9 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find g^{-1}(x) for g(x)=arcsin((1-x^2)/(1+x^2)), x>=0, justifying the choice of root.
method_path: Solve for y^2: y^2=(1+sin x)/(1-sin x)
Reject negative root because domain of g is x>=0 so range of g^{-1} is y>=0

evidence.basis: M1 x=arcsin((1-y^2)/(1+y^2)). A1 sin x=(1-y^2)/(1+y^2) => sin x + y^2 sin x = 1 - y^2. A1 y^2=(1+sin x)/(1-sin x). R1 positive root taken (domain of g is x>=0 so range of g^{-1} is y>=0). A1 g^{-1}(x)=sqrt((1+sin x)/(1-sin x)). [5 marks]

blocks.task_summary: State the domain of g^{-1}.
method_path: State domain as -pi/2 <= x < pi/2 or [-pi/2, pi/2)
accepted_alternatives: Accept [-pi/2, pi/2[ or [-1.57, 1.57) if correct to 3 s.f.

evidence.basis: domain is -pi/2 <= x < pi/2 A1. Accept correct alternative notations e.g. [-pi/2, pi/2[ or [-pi/2, pi/2). Accept [-1.57, 1.57) if correct to 3 s.f. [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Sketch the graph of y=g^{-1}(x), indicating asymptotes with equations and axes intercepts.
method_path: Sketch curve with domain [-pi/2, pi/2) and range [0, infinity)
Show asymptotic behaviour as x approaches pi/2 from below

evidence.basis: A1 for correct domain, correct range and y-intercept at y=1. A1 for asymptotic behaviour x->pi/2. A1 for x=pi/2. Coordinates not required. Do not accept x=1.57 or inexact values. [3 marks]
